implementation_notes: Go builds its route by decorating the destination handler: a Detour is a wrapper chosen at composition time from configuration (if cfg.DetourEnabled { h = Audit(h) }), or, for RPC, an extra interceptor appended to grpc.ChainUnaryInterceptor. Because there is no framework that rewrites the chain at runtime, the wrapper must call the handler it was given - that call is the rejoin to the same destination - and a live switch has to be an atomic.Bool (or a flag provider) read inside the wrapper. The same shape works for channel consumers: a Handler func(*Message) (*Message, error) wrapper around the delivery function.
pitfalls: A plain bool captured at wiring time yields a toggle nobody can flip at runtime; use atomic.Bool or a flag lookup for a live switch.
A wrapper that returns early instead of calling next silently drops the message rather than rejoining the flow.
Sharing one detour handler across goroutines means any state it keeps (replay buffers, counters) must be synchronised, or the detour races.
